analysis:
The changed file is a Swift test file (EngineV2BridgeTests.swift). The changes add a decodeTable to StubTokenizer (~lines 146-155), thread a stopStringScope parameter into makeBridge (443, 462), and add tests (847-899) for matchedStopSequence with ReasoningStopScope. They cover scoped stop reporting for the Gemma4 and Qwen3 reasoning parsers and model-vs-request scope precedence. No production code is changed in the supplied units, so there is no new attack surface, no auth, attestation, encryption, or billing path change, and no change to the cache salt or tenant scoping logic.

The visible tests include a cache-scope test (bridgeStampsCacheSalt, ~761-785). It asserts that caller-controlled fields (promptCacheKey, user) never become cacheSalt. This is consistent with T-041's mitigation that scope is coordinator-authored, and the PR does not weaken that mitigation. The usage-max billing defense test (usageMaxDefense) is unchanged context.

The production change implied by these tests is the scoped matchedStopSequence logic in EngineV2Bridge. It is not supplied in these units. The main remaining question is whether that production logic reports the matched stop sequence correctly and without leaking reasoning content. The tests suggest it does, but it cannot be verified here. This is a correctness and telemetry concern for the next pass, not a demonstrated security regression. The matched stop sequence is stored in the usage signal. A downstream pass should check whether that value is user-supplied stop text only (the candidate caller sequence), not generated text, when it is sent over the wire.

No finding qualifies. A deeper review of the production EngineV2Bridge and ReasoningStopScope source is advisable only if integration finds them in scope.
